title: Golden Hour Calculator: Light for Photographers
description: Find morning and evening golden hour windows for any place and date with the Golden Hour Calculator — computed from the Sun's actual path. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, in New York on 21 June 2026 the evening golden hour runs about 19:48 to 20:50 (computed) — a full hour of low gold, because summer suns at that latitude set at a slant.
quick_answer: The Golden Hour Calculator finds the morning and evening windows when the Sun sits in the low band photographers love — roughly between 4 degrees below and 6 degrees above the horizon. Enter a place and date and read both windows, computed from solar position, not guessed.

faq: Is golden hour really an hour?

Rarely exactly. It is about twenty minutes near the equator, near an hour at mid-latitudes, and can stretch past two hours toward the poles in season — where, in midsummer, it can last all 'night'. The name is a souvenir from temperate latitudes.

Gold is the Sun just above (or barely below) the horizon throwing warm direct light; blue is the deeper band after it leaves, when the sky itself is the light source. This calculator's window edges touch the blue hour at its −4° boundary.
Which window is better, morning or evening?

The geometry is symmetric; the air is not. Mornings are often clearer and emptier of people; evenings carry the day's haze and warmth. Most photographers have a favourite and a superstition to defend it.
Does the calculator account for mountains or skyline?
No — it computes the astronomical window for a level horizon. A western ridge steals the last minutes; a tower shoots its shadow early. Local scouting adjusts the ends.
Why do dates near the solstice change so little?
The Sun's declination stalls near its extremes, so windows plateau for days around the solstices — and race near the equinoxes. Your favourite light returns almost identically for a solstice week.
Can I plan a sunrise shoot with it?
Yes — the morning window tells you when gold starts relative to sunrise (about 05:24 in the New York June example). Arrive in the blue before it; the calculator's job is that you know the minute.
Everything mirrors: December is the long-light solstice, June the short one. The calculator uses your coordinates, so Sydney and Cape Town get their own correct windows.
